key_insight: Human and LLM collaboration can accelerate materials synthesis by generating experimentally testable recipes, and it can even reveal previously unknown structures.
engineering_relevance: A closed-loop human–LLM workflow offers a practical route to speed up materials discovery and synthesis planning for next-generation functional materials.
method: Human and LLMs independently proposed synthesis recipes for known and unknown materials in the Ruddlesden-Popper family.
Recipes were executed in the lab and success was evaluated experimentally.
Results were fed back into a closed-loop process for a second round of collaboration.
evidence_signal: Across two rounds, humans and LLMs achieved similar lab success rates on known materials (83% vs 75% in round one; 79% vs 71% in round two) and lower but nonzero success on unknown targets (17% vs 22%; 22% vs 14%), enabling discovery of Ba3PtO5.
watch_item: Success on unknown materials remained modest, so lab validation and careful chemistry constraints are still essential before relying on generated recipes.
paper_title: Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery
